body.x: Switching power supplies, LED lighting and home appliances need protection against voltage surges, and the protection parts compete for space on circuit boards that keep getting smaller.

Huizhou Jingqin Electronic Components Co., Ltd, a national high-tech enterprise established in 2013 and led by Du Wentai, makes surface-mount (SMD) circuit protection components. Its R&D headquarters is in Shenzhen and its mass production base is in the Zhongkai High-tech Zone in Huizhou, where the factory began production in 2019. At KES 2026, the company is exhibiting SMD varistors, SMD NTC thermistors, SMD Y capacitors and SMD X capacitors, and offering on-site technical consultation and component sample evaluation.

The company says its patented multi-chip parallel and series structures help customers reduce PCB board space, improve surge resistance and make mass production more consistent compared with conventional discrete components. Its patents cover an SMD dual Y capacitor structure, a multi-chip parallel SMD Y capacitor, a multi-chip parallel and series SMD NTC thermistor, an SMD X capacitor structure and a 3-pin SMD Y capacitor. The products serve LED lighting, switching power supplies, industrial equipment, 5G base stations, consumer electronics, home appliances and automotive electronics.

Jingqin reported annual turnover of KRW 46.4 billion (about USD 33 million) in 2025, up 38% from the previous year, with repeat customers accounting for 70% of sales. In China, it supplies more than 40 manufacturers in power supply, lighting and home appliances. Since 2021, it has expanded to South Korea, India and Southeast Asia, and its 2025 export revenue reached KRW 14.9 billion, about 32% of sales, from more than 25 overseas OEM and ODM manufacturers. The factory holds IATF 16949 certification, and its products carry UL, KC, TUV, ENEC and CQC certifications.

The company's priority markets are South Korea, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. It is looking for local power supply and lighting OEMs and ODMs, as well as distributors that can offer sample testing and technical after-sales service, and it hopes to win well-known Korean OEM and ODM reference customers at the show. Jingqin aims to raise its export share from 32% to 42% by 2027 and plans to strengthen local technical support for Korean and Southeast Asian customers from the second half of 2026. It names a lack of efficient channels to find reliable overseas distributors and the difficulty of building local after-sales support as its main challenges.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
